EW is the military action involving the use ofelectromagnetic energy to determine, exploit, reduce or prevent hostile use of the electromagnetic spectrum and action to retain its effective use by friendlyforces.The components of EW are: EW = ESM (passive offensive) + ECM (active offensive) + EPM (defensive)a.Electronic Warfare Support Measures (ESM).ESM is the principal information gathering and target identification activity of EW. It finds and exploits enemy transmissions and the location of emitters. This applies to both communications and non-communications (radars, lasers etc) transmissions.b.Electronic Counter Measures (ECM).ECM is the prevention of the enemy's use of the electromagnetic spectrum by Electronic Jamming and the use of other forms of Electronic Attack to influence his activities. It is the offensive and active arm of EW and is used to fix and to strike at the enemy.c.Electronic Protective Measures (EPM).EPM is the protection of friendly communications and non-communications systems against the enemy's attempts to find, fix and strike at them.

That part of an amphibious force that assaults or in the case of minor operations; goes ashore. In a major operation, it should consist of an all arms group and it can expect fire support and logistic support from ships, aircraft and helicopters. The size and grouping of the embarked forcewill depend on the operation and the recourses available.
EMCON provides selective and controlled use of electro-magnetic, acoustic or other emitters, to optimise command and control while minimizing detection and exploitation of an enemy's sensors.
A well-fortified gun position or machine gun nest.
Documents which are complete in themselves and sent with a covering document.
The clearing of opposition either by the Vanguard orAdvance Guard.

Forcing a passage across a water obstacle lightlyheld by the enemy, off the line of march. Momentum of the advance is thusmaintained. Speedy recce, good engineer intelligence and correct groupingof forces are essential for success. Also known as 'hasty crossing'.
End State is that state of affairs which needs to be achieved at the end of a campaign either to terminate the conflict or resolve it on favourableterms.
In air defence, a fire control order used to direct or authorise units and/or weapon systems to fire on a designated target.

An offensive action at formation and above level in which the main attack strikes the enemy from the rear. Essentially involves an outflanking movement which passes round or through the enemy positions to cut off his withdrawal routes, line of maintenance and destroy him. Alternatively, the movement may be two-pronged, one element to block the enemy from the front. Envelopment may be single or double:a.Single.Manoeuvre against one flank or around one flank against the rear of the initial disposition of the enemy.b.Double.Otherwise called encirclement. This is envelopmentfrom both flanks simultaneously.
All non-expendable items needed to outfit or equip an individual or organisation.

A location usually in or near the forward BAAwhere equipment casualties from units and LADs are collected before back loading by second line recovery resources. It is often convenient to locate it near the FRG (Forward Repair Group).
Any person who after physical capture by the enemy successfully escape into an area under own, friendly or neutral control.
Escarpment is an extended line of cliffs. That is, ground with sheer drop on one side.
A combatant unit(s) assigned to accompany and protect another force or convoy.

That relationship existing in a unit, formation or corps borne out of pride and confidence by all ranks belonging to that unit, formation or corps to the extent that the average soldier believes himself fortunate to belong to a particular unit and feels rather sorry for those soldiers who do not belong. Esprit-de-corps considerably enhance discipline. This is because theindividual is even more ready to sacrifice his own interests for the commongood.
Covert means of obtaining information of the enemy or potential enemy including his future strategic plans.

A logical process of reasoning by which a commander considers all the circumstances affecting the military situation and arrives at a decision as to the course of action to be taken in order to accomplish his mission. The types of Estimate Process are:a.The Operational Estimate.The Operational Estimate is designed for a JTFC at the operational level to develop his campaign plan and the subsequent modification of operation orders and directives. The estimate must be command-led, since it is the JTFC's decision that the process supports. All other estimates, at any level should be designed to contribute to the Operational Estimate.b.The Tactical Estimate.The tactical estimate provides a process that can be used by formation headquarters conducting complex planning with time available, within the context of a campaign plan, and where the campaign planning concepts have been decided at the operational level by the JFHQ. As with the joint operational estimate, from which the process has been developed, the tactical estimate seeks to produce a winning concept through analysis that is focused by the JTFC's direction.c. The Combat Estimate.The Combat Estimate is also known as the 7- Questions combat estimate, it is used primarily at the lower tactical level for decision-making in battles and engagements when time is short. It allows the commander at the lower levels of command, especially in the heat of action to use his intuition and training, to compress his decision making to produce a workable plan.
The tidal mouth of a river. A section of a river meeting the sea.
The movement of human and equipment causalities out of the area of operations.

An event overlay is derived from the situation overlay; it shows graphically the Named Area of Interest (NAI) where key tactical events are likely to take place. Theidentification of these NAIs will prompt the tasking of RISTA to maintainsurveillance over these areas.
The replacement of clothing and stores items that are either damage or have outlived their usefulness, e.g.., military uniforms.

A point deployed by the highest HQ in anoperation to shorten the turnaround where the replenishment park is too far to the rear for second line transport to get there and back within twenty-four hours.

An exempt call is defined as a call to those stations normally designated by a collective or all stations call, less certain specifically exempted stations. It is used when a calling station wishes to call the majority, but not all of the stations associated with a collective or all stations call. Exempt calls can simplify calls and prevent unnecessary replies.
A military manoeuvre or simulated wartime operation involving planning, preparation and execution. It is carried out for the purpose oftraining and evaluation.
An offensive operation that usually follows a successful attack and is designed to disorganise the enemy in depth. See ''Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach''.
Taking full advantage of success in battle and following up initial gains.
Taking full advantage of any information that has come to hand for tactical or strategic purposes.
All ammunition containing explosives, nuclear,biological and chemical agents including improvised explosive devices and all similar or related items or components that are explosive in nature.
The detection, identification, field evaluation, rendering safe, recovery and final disposal of unexploded explosive ordnance.
A form of positional defence employed on a wide front. It is characterized by large gaps, limited mutual support, greater depth of position and a strong reserve.
In amilitary operation, extraction is the urgent removal of an individual or a group of individuals or materiel from a threat.
The time designated for the start of FLOT aviation operations.
A facility for transmitting a document e.g., map, table or diagram over a voice circuit.
To dismiss a soldier(s) from a superior officer's/NCO's imm presence.
Radioactive materials deposited on the surface of the earth following the explosion of nuclear weapons, not only in the immediate vicinityof the explosion but over any region of the globe.

That degree of dominance in the air battle of oneforce over another, which permits the conduct of operations by the former and its related land, sea and air forces at a given time and place, withoutprohibitive interference by the opposing air force.
The purpose of a feint attack is to distract the action of an enemy force by seeking contact with it.

Medical unit that provides second line medical cover to units, it is allocated on a scale of one per brigade. It is fully mobile on organic transport and carries sufficient tentages to enable it work in the field whensuitable buildings are not available.In war, a field ambulance normally establishes one dressing station; the Main Dressing Station (MDS), wherecasualties receive treatment, are documented and prepared for future evacuation. The MDS in this case is normally sited in the fwd BAA. Sometimes however, in order to meet operational exigencies, a field ambulance can as an exception, provide two dressing stations, the MDS and the Advance Dressing Station (ADS).This is to cover long communication lines characteristic of the Advance and Withdrawal operations of war. In this case, it is normal for the ADS to be located in the fwd BAA and the MDS in the BAA.
Branch of artillery that is concerned with finding andengaging ground targets with indirect fire support of infantry and armour.Provides 'Close Support' and General Support.

The basic field training given to an individual soldier to enable is take his proper place in the military team under operational conditions. It includes the basic fundamentals of fire and movement, observationjudging distance, seeing without being seen and hearing without being heard andcamouflage and concealment. It also includes how to make the best possible use of cover and how to move with weapons and equipment.
An area in which it will be possible to fire effectively from a given position and which is related to a particular weapon.
Postal facility established in the Combat Zone.

Field signals are alternative means of passing orders and controlling troops by the use of hands, limbs, weapons and whistle when voice control is not possible owing to; battle noises, need for silence and intervening distances being too much for effective voice control.
Aircraft used for close air support mission.

Fighting power defines an army ability to fight. It isexpressed in qualitative terms, reflecting the suitability for employment in a particular environment of operations. Fighting power is made up of 3 components; conceptual, physical and moral components.a.Conceptual Components.This can be described as the thought process behind the ability to fight. It is made up of Principles of war, military doctrine and development.b.The Moral Component.The moral component concerns with the ability to get people to fight. It will involve; motivation, leadership and management.c.The Physical Component.The physical component is the means to fight. It is the equivalent of the term'combat power'(see'combat power').Physical componentincludesthe following elements; manpower, equipment, logistics/sustainability, training and readiness.

Area close to the objective where assaulting troops,it not already so deployed adopt their formation for the final assault. It may not be possible to lay down the precise positions at orders and is more likely to be indicated by radio or verbally during the attack.
See Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach.

The principle of having one 'leg' on the groundproviding security and providing fire or being ready to fire, while the other 'leg' moves (i.e., one leg up, one down). The idea is to ensure a proper balanceand close coordination of fire power (including air support) with the tactical mobility of the combat arms for the successful execution of a ground battle.

FCA is an area subject to specific restraintsinto which fire support in excess of those restraints (weight of fire, types of ammo etc) will not be delivered without the prior approval of the authorityestablishing the restraint.
'Fire for effect' means produce the full weight of fire requested in initial orders. This term is applicable to indirect fire and is issued after satisfactory ranging.
Initial warning order when requesting for fire, transmitted over the radio by an observer (supported arm, e.g. Infantry) to an OP officer (Artyofficer to whom fire request is made).
Specific assignment given to a fire unit as part of a definite plan.
Plan involving the dovetailing of available supporting firerecourses (including tank fire) to achieve the best possible utilization of theweapons in support of a unit or formation.

A Cell where detailed planning, control andcoordination of fire support is carried out at battalion group level. The FSC is supervised by the BC of the Direct Support battery who advises the battaliongroup commander on all fire support matters.The BC is assisted by the support company commander or mortar platoon commander. The FSC is also responsible for air safety within the battalion group air space and might include a forward air controller (FAC).

A line established by theappropriate ground commander to ensure coordination of fire not under hiscontrol but which may affect current tactical operations.The FSCL is used tocoordinate fire of air, ground or sea weapon systems using any type ofammunition against surface targets.
Measure taken to coordinate the fire of disparate fire units and to minimise fratricide.
Fire trench is that part of a battle trench from which the enemy may be observed and engaged.

The minimum number of weapons that can be employed on anyone serial of a fire plan. Below this level, fire is considered largely ineffective. A fire unit may be:a. One field battery (but four guns can be used for a smoke serial and only two for illumination).b. A troop of a medium battery (because of their heavier shells).c. A platoon of tanks.d. Two fighter ground attack (FGA) aircraft.

The quantity of C sups which is normally held by a unit on first line (i.e., organic) transport. It iscalculated to sustain that units in operations for a specific length of time without re-supply. It is controlled by the unit commander. If unit transport cannot carry the first line scale, the balance is either dumped in or near the unit's location or carried by second line transport.
Vehicle made according to specifications to carryradios and operate as vehicular stations, e.g., FFR Land Rover.
See ''Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach''.
A tactical obstacle effect that integrates fire planning and obstacle effort to slow down an attacker within a specified area, normally an engagement area.

A fixed line is a given line and point of aim on which a weapon is capable of firing from during mist, darkness or under poor visibility. It is notnecessary for the target to be visible when a weapon is set on fixed line as the weapon is so sited that its fire is effective on a selected area of ground. Fire onfixed line is opened on a pre-arranged signal order.

A foot march by soldiers (sometimes displaying military hardware including AFVs) in a civilian environment either to sell the military profession to civilians or in a CRW environment to serve as a deterrent topotential troublemakers
A security element operating to the flank of a moving or stationary force to protect it from enemy ground observation, direct fire, and surprise attack.
The means by which enemy interference by fire or assault onto the flanks of own force(s) is dealt with.
Direct fire weapons with line of sight aiming e.g., 107mm Anti-Tank gun etc.
This is a table (Relative Strength Table) comparing the strength of friendly and threat forces, at agreed intervals, to determine whether or not a force has achieved desired norms.
Foreshore is that portion of the shore between high and low watermarks.

Fording is the movement of a vehicle on the bed of awaterobstacle. A certain amount of preparation is usually carried out on the vehicle,depending on the depth of the water. For tanks and AFVs, fording may be:a.Shallow.No preparation is required for the vehicle. Top of the engine compartment and exhaust opening remain outside the water.b.Medium.Water level is up to turret ring. Preliminary preparations like sealing the top of the engine compartment and fitting special one-way valves on the exhaust are required. The driver will have to be directed by the tank commander.c.Deep.Otherwise called immersed fording or snorkelling. The tank is completely submerged. Air forintake by the engine and breathing by crew is introduced by snorkel apparatus. The drivermaintains direction by gyrocompass or by guidance via the radio, from outside.
Brigade, division and corps are all referred to individually as formation.
The last position occupied by the assault echelonbefore crossing the start line/line of departure.
An officer, warrant officer or senior NCO who from a forward ground or air position, directs the action of combat aircraft engaged in offensive close air support of land force.

Area which contains battalion A2 echelons and in addition may contain elements of logistic units,some of which would be under divisional control, which must be deployed in the brigade area in order to operate efficiently, e.g., DP. All units in the fwd BAA are controlled by the brigade HQ.

FEBA is the foremost limit of areawhere ground combat troops are deployed, excluding areas which the covering troops/screening forces are operating, designated to coordinate firesp and positioning of forces or the manoeuvre of units.
FLOT is the line which indicates the most fwd positions of friendly forces in any kind of military operations at a specific time.

A secure base, port or airfield, from whichan operation may be launched. It is normally, but not necessarily, external to the theatre of operations and may be an essential stepping-stone into thattheatre.
The Arty Officer in an OP, when the OP is mobile, e.g., in an advance, a field battery produces 3 FOOs.

An area providing a semi-permanent firm base from which offensive action against the insurgents can be developed. It should be established at a seat of local government as, a formation base, usually at brigade level, and will normally have a Tactical Transport (Medium range or short range) airfield, capable of quick development.

An operation in which a force advances or attacks through another force which is in contact with theenemy. The force in contact remains in place and must provide the advancing force with as muchassistance as possible including tactical and logistical support. A forward passage of lines will be used when:a.An attack is to be continued with fresh or more suitable forces.b.The force to be relieved is closely engaged with the enemy.c.The advancing force has to take possession of suitable terrain in order to continue the battle.

An area under cover in the vicinity of an objective to which tanks go when released from dominating the objective, and from which they are immediately available to return to fire positions or to support counterattacks.

A repair organization provided by an armoured or infantry workshop to carry our priority second line repairs in forward units. The FRG is based on forward repair teams (FRT) - four FRTs forinfantry workshops, considerably more for armoured workshops. The FRG is formed by adding elements from the MT platoon and the stores section NAOCto the FRTs provided by the repair company.
A workshop repair section of up to 50 men formed by base workshop and deployed usually to carry out unit and field repairs in an emergency.

Repair elements of the FRG that carry out priority tasks like replacement of major assemblies in forward units locations. Each FRT consist of up to four tradesmen mounted in a vehicle capable oflifting major assemblies up to three tones for an armoured workshop and up to one tone for an Infantry workshop.

These are the 4 fundamental questions which need to beaddressed if logistic requirements are to be assessed they are the start point.of all CSS planning. These are:Destination,Demand,DistanceandDuration.a.Destination.The destination sets the overall environment in which the operation is to take place,which determines the conditions for the pattern of wear and tear on equipment, the physiological demands on troops and define the strategic L of C.b.Demand.Demand encompasses the rate of consumption and usage of materiel, it stems directly from the commander's intent.c.Distance.Distance req consideration not only of the strategic L of C, but also of that within the theatre before, during and after the operation. The length, capacity and topography of the L of C will determine the size, shape, structure and balance of the CSS resources committed to it.d.Duration.The length of operations and rate of demand will determine the overall volume of materiel necessary or the size of the logistic problem. It will specify the endurance requirements, the needto rotate or replace equipment and men, and medical holding policies.

A FragO may be written, graphical/schematic,oral or a combination of these methods. It is used to supplement or amend an operation order. It should follow the same paragraph format as the orderwhich it is to supplement or amend. Where there is ''no change'' to a paragraph it must be annotated as such.
Fratricide is the unintentional killing or wounding of friendly personnel by fire.
An offensive manoeuvre in which the main effort is directed against the front of the enemy force(s).
This is combat order (see) plusrucksack and is a load which will be required for an operation of up to twoweeks duration without resupply except for ammunition, rations and water.
A command based on military functions ratherthan geographic areas.
The authority vested in a commander of one of the Services, a specialist agency or MOD branch acting on behalf of aServiceBoard.

Functions in Combat are practical conceptualtools deduced from principles of war required to implement ManoeuvristApproach to operations. The 6 principal functions in combat are:a.Information and Intelligence.Accurate and timely intelligence is fundamental to the success of all operations. Much of this information is derived from Reconnaissance, Intelligence, Surveillance and Target Acquisition (RISTA).b.Manoeuvre.To manoeuvre is to seek to get into a position of advantage in respect of the enemy from which force can be threatened or applied.c.Firepower.Firepower destroys, neutralises and suppresses; it is essential in defeating an enemy's ability to fight.d.Protection.Protection preserves the fighting potential of a force so that it can be applied at a decisive time and place.e.Combat Service Support (CSS).CSS sustains the force. It is the support provided to combat forces primarily in the fields of personnel and logistics.f.Command.Command is the exercise of authority and direction by a designated commander for the planning, direction, coordination and control of a military force.
The day and/or time on which an order (normally national) is given to deploy a unit.

Military gamble is an operation which can lead either to victory or the complete destruction of one's force. It is an operation of great risk, for instant, when defeat is imminent and gaining time is pointless, the only chance left is a ''gamble''.

Five and ten tone trucks required to move men and materials from the rear areas into the Combat Zone. It is from these transport resources that ST companieswill move combat supplies forward from RP to XP and further to the DP.

That support which is given to the supportedforce as a whole and not to any particular sub-division thereof. Often used to refer to artillery which is used to influence the corps or divisional battle andnormally tasked for counter battery and other depth targets. There is no guarantee of fire to the manoeuvre arm.

Gen Sp Rft artillery has the mission of supporting the forces as a whole and, on a secondary basis, ofproviding reinforcing fire for another artillery unit. Artillery allocated in this role has two priorities: the first is to the Comd Arty and the second is to thesupported formation. It provides therefore a certain degree of guaranteed fire though it is likely to have an ammunition caveat.
An unrestricted conflict between major powers. This might include widespread use of nuclear, chemical and possibly biological weapons.
Those regulations governing the treatment and handling of prisoners of war (POWs). POWs are expected to be treated firmly, fairly and humanely.
The systematic killing of all the people from a national, ethnic, or religious group, or an attempt to do this.

In conducting IPB,''Go'' areas are grounds which are open and suitable for manoeuvre. It must be assessed according to the type of force, forexample, what is ''Go'' to the dismounted forces might not be ''Go'' to the armour or mounted forces.
A gorge is a deep narrow valley which is rugged and usually rocky.

See 'Strategy'Grid.Grid is a system of squares formed by lines, which representing progressive distances EAST and NORTH of a fixed point.Grid Bearing.The direction of an object from a point, expressed as an angle (degree or mil) measured clockwise with reference to grid north.Ground of Tactical Importance (GTI).GTI is the ground the possession of which by the end willseriously interfere with the successful def of the position.

There are three types of ground manoeuvreforces: Heavy, medium and light. They will usually operate in combination.a.Heavy Forces.Heavy forces are basically heavy armoured fighting vehicles, they utilise automotive power to deploy considerable firepower, protection and battlefield mobility. Although, their use is restricted in some complex terrain, and their operational and strategic mobility is constrained by weight and logistic requirements, they still form a major component of many land forces.b.Medium Forces.Medium forces are basically light armoured vehicles they are strategically and operationally more deployable than heavy forces, and may be among the first elements to deployinto a theatre.c.Light Forces.Light forces are basically foot infantry troops, they have significant strategic mobility, since they can be transported by aircraft to any theatre. They may be the only forces that canoperate in complex terrain. However, their firepower is limited compared to heavy or medium forces, and they are vulnerable. Provision of greater mobility or firepower (APC) gives them the characteristics of medium forces, but may reduce their strategicmobility and utility.

The plan to coordinate the employment of patrols, Ops, FOO and MFC zones of observations, aerial recce and surveillance devices. This is to enable the commander watch the battlefield at all times and gather combat intelligence in time for him to react and retain the initiative.
The point on the ground surface vertically beneath or above which a nuclear weapon has exploded. Maximum damage from the nuclear explosion will be recorded on the Ground Zero.
Combined arms training from company group level.
Allotment of arms and services under one commander for a task.

This is the division of a battlegroup into functional groupsto achieve effective concurrent activity prior to an operation, The compositionof each group will vary according to the task, as explained below:a.Reconnaissance Group (R Group).The RG ro up is responsible for reconnaissance and planning. The group includes those necessary to give the appropriate advice, a security element and communications.b.Orders Group (O Group).The O Group receives orders and contains all those with a part to play in the forthcoming operation. From these orders, recipients extract the appropriate information and issue their own orders. may undertake preliminary moves, whilst orders are being written and given.d.Harbour and Rear Recce Parties.If the main body has to move forward to a concentration or assembly area, a harbour party will be despatched ahead of the main body. Its tasks will be to recceand lay out the new area and then to guide the main body, as they arrive, to their positions. If it is necessary for a battlegroup to withdraw, it is usual to despatch a rear recce group. This group combines a tactical reconnaissance function with that of the normal harbour party in the event of having to fight from this position upon their arrival.
Guards are covering troops deployed to delay the en for a specifiedperiod, additional to observation and report on en movement.
Tank designated for 'sentry' tasks in a combat team leaguer.The tank remains fully manned for the period it so designated.

Military or Para-military operations conducted in enemy held or hostile territory by irregular, predominantly indigenous force. Guerrillawarfare will be the main preoccupation of security forces in counter insurgency.

Weapons in which the projectiles are remotely guided by an external mechanism onto a target after firing. In some cases, the weapons are fed with relevant dataand the projectiles take over the guidance automatically and home on to their targets.

a. The specific time at which an operation or exercise commences or is due to commence. It is also the time at which the Line of Departure (LD) is crossed by the leading elements in an attack.b. In amphibious operations, the time at which the first waterborne wave of an amphibious assault lands on the beach.
Hachuring is a conventional method of representing hill features by short disconnected lines drawn directly down the slope in the direction of the flow of water on the slopes.
A control feature, preferably following easily definedterrain features, at which responsibility for the conduct of combat operations is passed from one force to another.

An area well out of contact where a force lie up for any length of time for administrative convenience (e.g. refit, rest, reorganization and maintenance). Protection and concealment will be maintained.

A party formed when required for a specific task, e.g. recce and planning of a new harbour area (See ''Grouping System''). On completion of the task, members rejoin their normal echelons. At battalion level, it will be commanded by the 2ic and will include representatives of the company groups and specialist subunits.
In land operations, an attack in which preparation time is traded for speed in order to exploit an opportunity.
The rapid creation of a route through a minefield, barrier or fortification by any expedient method.
The crossing of an inland water obstacle using thecrossing means at hand or those readily available and made without pausing for elaborate preparations.

A defence normally organised while in contact with the enemy or when contact is imminent and time available for the organisation is limited. It is characterised by improvement of the natural defensive strength of the terrain by utilisation of foxholes, emplacements, and obstacles.

The word headquarters is often used as a generic term for the grouping of the staff, its associated CIS and a structure which provides a working environment. There are 6 types of headquarters and they are described below:a.Main Headquarters (Main).As the name implies this is the central controlling headquarters (at any level) where all the staff functions of that headquarters are coordinated and where thecommand and control of all subordinate units is focussed. The headquarters itself is normally commanded by the COS who decides on its composition, organisation, siting and tactical deployment.b.Forward Headquarters (Fwd HQ).This is usually an advance or detached element of the HQ, perhaps deployed early into theatre, with a skeleton communications infrastructure and very limited protection. It would typically be mounted in soft-skinned vehicles. Fwd HQ lacks the resources to support command in battle.c.Tactical Headquarters (Tac HQ).All field headquarters requireto be tactical. If a headquarters has become too large and unwieldy, then its structure should be pruned. Tac HQ refers to a small HQ (Comd and principal Arms Advisers as appropriate) complete withsufficient mobility, protection and communications to command the battle for limited periods away from Main.d.Alternate Headquarters (Alt HQ).Alternate headquarters provide continuity of command when a headquarters either needs to be moved or is put out of action.e.Step-Up Headquarters (Step-Up).If fewer vehicles, manpower and CIS are available, a Step-Up headquarters may replicate only key functions and be capable of holding control for only limited periods while a Main headquarters moves and while men andvehicles are transferred from the previous Main headquarters location.f.Rear Headquarters (Rear).The principal location for the designated commander of any rear operations including combat service support activity.

Hide is a concealed position in which a force waits before operation or before moving into battle position. A subunit hide should provide:a. Overhead protection (OHP) and concealment against en action and observation.b. All round defence.c. Dispersion.d. Easy access and breakout.
HPTs are those targets/assets whoseacquisition and successful attack will contribute substantially to the successof the friendly commander's mission.
A HPTL is a list of HPTs in priority.
HVTs are those targets/assets which the enemycommander requires for the successful completion of his mission and are,therefore, of high value to him.

Hold is applicable to both defence and attack.a.In defence.To hold is to maintain or retain possession of a position or an area by force.b.In an attack.Holding Attack is to exert sufficient pressure to hold the enemy in position to deceive him as to where the main attack is coming from. This is to prevent movement, re-disposition of enemyforces and also to prevents him from reinforcing his elements and /or to cause him to commit reserves prematurely at an indecisive location.

Homer is a process where an aircraft, using the homing facility, can home on to any VHF/FM station within range by getting the station to transmitvoice or a carrier wave for short periods. Homing facility are used when a pilot has difficulty in locating a station on theground. Homing indications will only be seen while the ground station is transmitting.
The distance measured on the map betweenadjacent contours or between two points.

Civil and military assistance rendered inpeace and war by a host nation to allied forces which are located on or in transit through the host nation's territory. The basis of such assistance is commitments arising from bilateral or multilateral agreements concluded between the host nation and the nation(s) having forces operating on the hostnation's territory.
A gun with a high angle (450800) capability, giving it the same ability as mortars in engaging targets on reverse slopes, etc.
Normal tank position for direct fire, only the turret is visible to the enemy.
A system using electromagnetic transmissions to which equipment carried by friendly forces automatically responds, for example by emitting pulses, thereby distinguishing themselves from enemy forces
The use of white light at any stage of a night attack.

II is a passive device used to make objects visible indarkness. The II principle basically involves the use of ambient light to intensify the image of the objects electronically, thereby making the objects visible.

Air support to meet specific requests which ariseduring the course of a battle, and which by their nature cannot be planned in advance as opposed to pre-planned air support for which notification is madein advance (normally forty-eight hours in advance).
Ground that is highly desirable rather than essentialto hold.

An imprest account is the account maintained in acommand into which all public funds released to the command to meet expenditure under the approved Army allocation is paid. The purpose of imprest account is to record receipts and subsequent expenditure of the funds into it.

Implies the fire or locating effort of the arty unitis normally guaranteed and arty liaison is provided at every level of command (e.g. FOO at Coy level, BC at Bn-level, etc). Thus an arty unit or subunit canonly be placed in direct support of one battalion group or formation. Arty in direct support provides:a. Advice and communication to the supported arm.b. Observation (if applicable) to the front and flanks.c. Guaranteed fire support from its guns.
An expression used to denote the task of providing artillery supporting fire to a formation or unit. Liaison and observation are not normally provided.

All forms of training of the soldier, NCO, warrant officer and officer as an individual to enable each take his proper place and play his part adequately in his arm or service. Some of the aspects of individualtraining in the infantry for example include physical fitness training, shooting and weapon handling, communication skills, helicopter drills, preparation offire and shelter trenches and overhead protection, night training, AFV and aircraft recognition, field craft, general knowledge, etc. Some of these aspects are common to all arms and services.
A methodical process of interrogation, discussion,propaganda and harassment designed to alter people's concepts and convictions and to condition them to accepting a new ideology or thinking.
The Infantry mission is 'to close with and engage the enemy in concert with other arms, through fire and manoeuvre in all operational theatres and environments, in order to bring about his defeat'
Modified APC that not only carries theinfantry to the battlefield, but also into it. The main modification is onincreased armament, thereby giving the infantry more teeth.
Telephone mounted at the rear of the hull of a tank tofacilitate infantry men from outside the tank speaking with individual tank commanders within. Not all tanks carry infantry telephones.
A technique and process in which a force moves asindividuals or small groups over, through or around enemy positions without detection

Unprocessed or 'raw' data which may either be used simply to inform about some matter or, which can be subjected to an analytical process, in order to assess a capability or predict what the outcome of an event may be.
INFOSEC is the security of InformationSystems (IS), including hardware, software and bearer systems. Particularattention should be paid to IS using commercial bearer systems, such as theInternet.
A person who provides information to a collection agency. See 'Sources and Agencies'.
A member of an organisation who passes information to the opponents of the organization.

Active night fighting device which enables the user to see in darkness, also called red light. The system depends upon emitting an IR beam which is invisible to the naked eye but when viewed through special IRviewing device appears as light. It can be detected by an enemy with an IR capability.

IRLS is a sensor employed by reconnaissanceaircraft to detect natural infrared radiation on the ground. It is of particular value in the jungle because of its ability to penetrate natural cover althoughwater vapour in the atmosphere tends to degrade the resolution obtained.
Any logistic or administrative base. This definition also includes POW camps.

An instruction is used to regulate military activity, itcomplement directives or orders. Examples are:a.Standing Instructions. Standing Instructions are issued typically to set out organisational responsibilities and to govern routine administrative procedures and actions.b.Periodic Instructions.Periodic Instructions cater for anyspecific actions required of a non-routine nature.c.Formal Instructions.Formal Instructions carry authorityequivalent to that of directives or orders.

A form of rebellion in which a dissident faction that has the support or acceptance of a substantial part of the population instigates thecommission of widespread acts of civil disobedience, sabotage and terrorism, and wages guerrilla warfare in order to overthrown a government. A state of insurgency implies that the insurgents have control of sizeable areas of the country and that it will almost inevitably be part of a revolutionary war on the communist pattern.

Insurgent is a term that can be used in place of any of these following terms when applicable, these are; guerrilla, revolutionary, terrorist, dissident, rioter, saboteur, enemy, insurrectionist or rebel.

When subject revolt they openly express their dissatisfaction with the established government or policies. When such an expression is armed and organized it becomes a rebellion. When a rebellion has a large measure of support and aims to overthrow the government a state of insurgency exists.
A prediction or assessment resulting from the collection, evaluation, analysis, integration and interpretation of all available information.

One of the methods of disseminating intelligencegiven in a set sequence to ensure that no important details are omitted. The intelligence briefing must include 'Comment' and an overall summary of enemy capabilities. The complete format is contained in appropriate service manuals appertaining to 'Intelligence'.

This is the process by which information is turned intointelligence and disseminated. It consists of 5 stages which, although cyclical in nature, may also take place concurrently. They are summarised as follows:a.Direction.The commander produces his intelligence requirements.b.Tasking.The G2 staff task appropriate sources and agencies with specific question.c.Collection.Sources and agencies collect information or provide intelligence.d.Processing.Information is collated, evaluated, analysed, integrated and interpreted by the G2 staff. The product of this processing is intelligence.e.Dissemination.Information and intelligence are passed or presented to those who need it.

A written appreciation by the intelligence staffconsidered solely from the enemy's point of view. The intelligence staff musttherefore 'think as the enemy thinks'. The estimate is made assuming theworst case, i.e., that the enemy is aware of our capabilities and intentions.The aim is to ultimately arrive at the most probable enemy COA in the givencircumstance.

IPB is a systematic and continuous process of analyzing environment in a specific geographic areaand the threat. IPB identifies critical battlefield decision points, so that Reconnaissance, Intelligence,Surveillance and Target Acquisition (RISTA) assets can be used to best effect, in order to assist the commander in making his decision. IPB has 3 main steps; these are battlefield area evaluation, threat evaluation and threat integration.

A non-routine report, initiated at any level,containing urgent information or intelligence that cannot await the next routine report. Whenever an interpretation of the information given in themassage is included, it should be preceded by the word 'Comment'.

A routine report initiated at brigade and above levels and contains all important items of information and intelligence within the period covered, including relevant negative information. It has no format except that:a. The text of an INTSUM is preceded by the abbreviation INTSUM.b. The intelligence staff's deduction is preceded by the word 'Comments'.
Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance(ISTAR).
Interception is the act of searching for, listening to and recording radio communications and electronic transmissions for the purpose of obtaininginformation.

A condition which exists when two or more itemspossess such functional and physical characteristics as to be equivalent in performance and durability, and are capable of being exchanged one for theother without alteration of the items or of adjoining items, except for adjustment and without selection for fit and performance.
Internal communications, by telephone or radio.May be within a HQ, an establishment, or a vehicle.
Actions to divert, disrupt, delay, or destroy the enemy before he can affect friendly forces.
The common bdry between a system or mode of op and a different system or mode.

Firing across another subunit's weapon fire. The aim is to ensure that the arcs of responsibility of the small arms of neighbouring subunits cross in order to avoidleaving a gap between sub units. Overlapping fire on the other hand takes care of the neighbouring subunits frontages.
In land warfare, an area or feature between the line of departure and an objective which must be seized or held.
A delaying position temporarily occupied by troops to cover a withdrawal and buy time to allow for the preparation and occupation of a new main defensive position.

Any military role which involves primarily themaintenance and restoration of law and order and essential services in the face of civil disturbances and disobedience, using minimum force. It coversaction dealing with minor civil disorders with no political undertones as well as riots devouring of revolts and even the early stages of rebellion.
Fixed and portable systems extensively used for speech and data transmission in nonhostileoperations e.g.humanitarian relief ops.

The ability of systems, units or forces to provide services to and accept services from other systems, units or forces and to use the services so exchanged to enable them to operate effectively together.
Questioning, mainly of POWs and suspects.
Those tanks in an infantry/tank attack which assault the objective with the infantry from a fire base using direct fire.
Offensive air operations by day or night over enemyterritory with the primary object of destroying enemy aircraft in the vicinity of their bases.
Flooding of an area to create an obstacle.
To lay a siege or dominate an area with a force and isolate it.

A tactical task given to a unit to seal off, both physically and psychologically, an enemy from his sources of support, deny him freedom of movement, and prevent his unit from having contact with other enemy forces.
Used by French speaking countries and means D-Day.
Jamming is the use of powerful transmissions to overwhelm an enemy receiver such that it is unable to receive wanted signals.

Javelin is a shoulder launched anti-aircraft system designed to intercept directly attacking targets. It has a minimum range of 500m, maximum ranges of 4.5 kms (against approaching aircraft) and 5.5 kms(against hovering helicopters) and a maximum effective height of 3,000 feet. It can only be fired dismounted and can only be used by day. The recentintroduction of ADAD has significantly improved the early warning and target acquisition capability of Javelin detachments.
The movement of tanks to alternative positions in order to:a.Avoid detection.b.Avoid being engagedc.Gain some other tactical advantage.

A JAAT operation is a coordinatedattack involving a combination of aviation and OAS aircraft, normally supported by artillery or naval gunfire and, where possible, by Electronic Warfare (EW) assets. The combination of these elements provides a highly mobile force with a destructive capability which, if used correctly, can considerably influence the course of the ground battle. The purpose of a JAAT is to provide a commander with a flexible combination of firepower that can be utilised quickly across the battlefield.
A force made up of more than one service (Army, Navy and Air force). In a CRW environment the police are inclusive
Operations involving more than one service (Army, Navy and Air force). This includes the police in a CRW setting.
Designated point at which in all types of combatunits/fmns must make contact for control and coordination.
The day on which the convoy system is introduced on any particular convoy lane.
A concentrated site or installation, the destruction orcapture of which would seriously affect the war effort or the success of operations. E.g., ammunition dump.

In IS operation KPs are the priority Vulnerable Point (VP) which is classified as key and for which a militaryguard should be provided. The classification may be for a limited period only. Examples are:a.Communication centre.b.Joint HQs.c.Public utilities such as power stations and waterworks.d.Bridge essential to the security forces.

A key terrain is any feature or area which the seizure or control offers a marked tactical advantage. Examples of key terrain features incl;bridges, fording site, high ground, choke points road junctions and survey control points.

An area in which a commander plans to force the enemy to concentrate, so as to destroy him with conventional or tactical nuclearweapons. The area or zones where nuclear weapons are primarily planned to be used are termed nuclear killing zones (NKZ).
A knoll is a low detached hill.

a.The time when troops cross the start line for phase 2 in a phased attack. L-Hour is therefore to be associated with attacks that are of more than one phase.b.In amphibious and airmobile operations, L Hour is the time at which the first helicopter of a heliborne assault wave touches down inthe landing zone.
A land force consists of combat, combat support,combat service support and command support elements. The proportion of each will vary between campaigns and operations.
Combat elements are those elements thatengage the enemy directly; they fight, typically employing direct-fire weapons. They include infantry, armoured and some aviation units.

Combat Service Support is 'the support provided to combat forces primarily in the fields of administration and logistics'. These force elements include logistic,medical and equipment support; personnel welfare; and administration. Others are force support engineers, they provide water and electrical power supply, construct infrastructure andmaintain supply routes.

Command Support elementsassist commanders in the exercise of command. They include staff of all types; communications, intelligence and information systems; andlife support elements to protect, sustain and move the commanderand his staff.
Seagoing craft which falls under the category ofamphibious shipping, designed to carry and land forces and their equipmentwith or without the use of aport.
A point within a landing site where one helicopter canland.

A site within a landing zone containing one or morelanding points. In amphibious operations,landing siteis a continuous segment of coastline over which troops, equipment and supplies can belanded by surface means.
Any specified zone used for the landing of aircraftincluding troop lift aircraft.
Obstacles laid across a frontage, the aim being tocut all routes through a zone extending across the enemy's line of advance,including any lateral routes which could be used to switch axes.
The latitude of a place is the area of the meridian from the place to equator expressed in degrees at the centre of the Earth.

Temporary position occupied by one withdrawingsubunit to cover the withdrawal of another. Essentially the principle of 'one leg up one leg down', applied to withdrawal operations. It is only applicable today withdrawal.
The art of influencing and directing men in such a manner as to obtain their willingness, loyalty, obedience and respect to accomplish amission.

A defended formation, sometimes concealed, adopted by a force for administrative convenience and protection. Usually associated witharmour. Leaguers may be close, with vehicles parked very near one another, or open, with vehicles wellspaced out.

Type of tactical movement used during mechanized and non mechanised operation. The rear vehicles/troops pass through the frontvehicles/troops on to the next fire position with the later providing covering fire. It is used where speed is essential andwhen enemy contact is not expected and risk can be taken.
Personnel who are exempted from full combatduty with their units.

There are 3 levels of war; they are strategic, operational, and tactical.a. The strategic level.This includes both the grand strategy and the military strategy. Grand strategy is the application of national resources to achieve policy objectives while military strategy is the application of military resources to achieve grand strategic objectives.b. The operational level.This extends from the level of a joint task force including the combined forces of naval, air power and ground operation to the manoeuvre brigade echelon.c. The tactical level.This extends from the manoeuvre brigade to the lowest fighting elements including individual soldiers.

Levee en masse are Inhabitants of a non-occupiedterritory, who on the approach of the enemy spontaneously and en masse take up arms to resist the invading forces, without having had time to formthemselves into organized armed units. Participants in a ''levee en masse'' are considered as combatants provided they carry arms openly and must respect the law of war.Leverage.Leverage inoperational art is gaining, maintaining, and exploiting advantages in combat power across all dimensions. Leverage allows joint force commanders to impose their will on the enemy, increase the enemy's dilemma, and maintain the initiative.

Liaison is defined as that contact or intercommunication maintained between elements of military forces and, where necessary, nonmilitaryagencies to ensure mutual understanding and unity of purpose andaction.

A liaison officer is an officer who is exchanged between two or more forces and is empowered to represent and make appropriate recommendations on behalf of his commander. He has to be prepared toamplify his commander's intent and points of detail whenappropriate. Moreover, a liaison officer shall assist his own commander through the timelyexchange of information, intentions, and situational awareness.
A designated line forward of which vehicles are required to use blackout lights at night.
International armed conflicts, short of general war. It may be limited geographically, by the scale of forces or by the weapons employed but will be conducted overtly by formations of regular troops.

Type of artillery fire in which shells fall along anapproximate line on any desired bearing, for example, along the line of a trench system or the front edge of a wood. This takes longer to arrange than a simple Concentration and the response to correction is slower. (See ''Concentration1''.)
A form of positional defence with little or no depth.
All the land, sea, and air routes that connect anoperating military force with one or more bases of operations, and along which supplies and reinforcements move.
In land warfare, a line designated to coordinate thedeparture of attack elements.

Lines of Logistic Support refer to the level at which logistic support is controlled; they are as follows:a.First Line.Support integral to units; that is A and B echelon see ''Echelon'' for details.b.Second Line.Support within the division less first line. This encompasses CSS at both brigade and divisional level. In general, second line close support is found at the brigade level, and second line general support at divisional level.c.Third Line.In-theatre support to the rear of the division.
Lines of operation describe how military force is applied in time and space through decisive points on the path to the enemy centre ofgravity.

Link-Up operations are conducted to join two friendlyforces in enemy controlled territory. It may therefore be necessary to destroy the enemy between these forces before a link-up can be established. Bothforces maybe moving towards one another, or one may be stationary.

This is a location statement in the field, whichmust always be submitted by all units and formations immediately after every move, to the next higher HQ. A LOCSTAT must always show the exact location of the HQ originating the LOCSTAT and the HQ and/or area centre point of its subordinate formations or units. It is expressed as a sixfigure gridreference.
It is the deviation of the magnetic needle ofcompass from its main position, owing to the presence of masses of magnetic iron ore or of iron in the neighbourhood.

Logging is the most important part of a watch keeper's job. It involves the recording of information in a prescribed manner on log sheets.The order of recording or reporting information is as follows:a. Time (When?) - At 2220 hours.b. Place (Where?) - At grid 654321.c. Activity (What?) - Tank noise heard.d. Action taken - IRONSIDE to contain.

The science of planning and carrying out the movement and maintenance of forces. Logistics in its most comprehensive sense involve those aspects of military operations which deal with:a.Design and development, acquisition, storage, movement,distribution, maintenance, evacuation, and disposition of materiel.b.Movement, evacuation, and hospitalisation of personnel.c.Acquisition or construction, maintenance, operation, and disposition of facilities.d.Acquisition or furnishing of services.e.Medical and Health Service support.
A shortened form of instructions showing details of logistic support available to a formation.

A long message is defined as any message that will take longer than 20 seconds to transmit. Long messages are divided into convenient sections to allowfor satisfactory reception in manageable stages,and to permit the transmission of more urgent traffic.
The longitude of a place is the angle at the pole between the meridian of that place and standard meridian (that of Greenwich).
Lost is a situation where the fall of shots or rounds fired by a gun, mortar or tank (main armament) is unobserved.
Low Intensity conflict is a term often used in placeof Civil Disorder and Revolutionary War.
The day on which mobilization commences or is due to commence.
A store or place authorized for the storage of explosive and ammunition.
Magnetic Meridian is a magnetic NORTH andSOUTH line.
It is the angle between the true NORTH and themagnetic NORTH. It is called EAST and WEST variation according to whether the magnetic North is East or West of the true NORTH.
A large area containing the complex organization which gathers together the men and material needed to maintain the activities of armed forces engaged in war.

Main Effort is the concentration of forces or means, in a particular area, where a commander seeks to bring about a decision. It is a concept or 'tool' to provide a focus for the activity which a commander considers crucial to the success of his mission. The decision on where to establish the Main Effort will depend on the higher commander's Intent, the commander's mission analysis, the relative strengths and the intelligenceavailable.
The route or routes designated within an areaof operations upon which the bulk of traffic flows in support of military operations.

All supply and repair action taken to keep a force in condition to carry out its mission. It is the routine recurring work required to keep a facility (plant, building, structure etc) in such a condition that it maybe continuously utilised, at its original or designed capacity and efficiency, for its intended purpose.

The technique of handling and controlling men in order to achieve high morale in a unit. It involves the following aspects:a. Good leadership, including welfare of men.b. Discipline.c. Religion, to give troops the necessary spiritual uplifts.d. Having an ideal, thereby 'knowing the reason why'.e. The professional skills of the soldier.f. Esprit''“de-corps and tradition.
Employment of forces on the battlefield through movement in combination with fire, or fire potential, to achieve a position of advantage in respect to the enemy in order to accomplish the mission.
An area clear of mines or other obstacles and sufficiently wide to allow forces to manoeuvre within or pass through it, in its tactical formation.

Manoeuvre Support are those activities, primarilymilitary engineering, which contribute to shaping the battle space to enable strategic, operational and tactical freedom of manoeuvre across the continuum of operations.

The manoeuvrist approach is that approach tooperations in which shattering the enemy's overall cohesion and will to fight is paramount. It calls for an attitude of mind in which doing the unexpected, using initiative and seeking originality is combined with a ruthless determination to succeed.

A map is a plan view of the ground, drawn or not drawn to scale, showing the details existing on the ground. There are 4 types of maps, they are:a.Cadastral Maps.These are large scale maps which cover relatively small areas, but gives detailed information concerning the features of the area that is represented. Cadastral maps give details of natural features like relief, vegetation, drainage and other manmade features like settlement, communication lines, and cultivation and so on.b.Sketch Maps.Sketch maps are in most cases, rough maps not drawn to scale. They are often called plans, and drawn without regard to details of accuracy as they are often drawn free hand.c.Distribution Maps.These are maps drawn from information obtained from geographical data, usually of such elements as weather or climate, population, crops or minerals. Distribution maps provide very useful information that can be easily interpreted and so they are very useful for the purpose of regional planning.d.Atlas Maps.Atlas maps are small scale maps that represent very large areas ranging in size from localized region such as a local government area, to a state, a continent or even the whole world. Atlas maps cover large areas, therefore, they are drawn to small scales and they do not necessarily contain as much detailed information about the area as cadastral maps.

Martial law is a condition that exists when disorder has reached such proportions that the normal legal processes of the state cannot function any longer and the only organization that can impose any authority isthe armed forces, by force of its arms. A state of martial law involves the suspension or ordinary law and its replacement by military rule.

All stores and equipment required by a force for an undertaking.It includes:a. Combat Supplies (C Sups) ''˜See'.b. Ordnance Stores 'See'.c. Vehicles 'See'.d. Engineer and Defence Stores.e. Specialist Medical and Dental Equipment Stores.
Infantry borne in armoured personnel carriers(APCs) thereby gaining increased protection added mobility and more firepower.
Form of warfare in which all the combat elements aremounted in armoured vehicles.
Mediation is when a third party assists by acting between opposed parties in an effort to bring them together.
Small medical detachment, lower to an MRS instatus, which provide first line medical cover to the unit or subunit to which it is attached.

Meeting engagement is a combat action that mayoccur when both sides seek to fulfil their mission by offensive action. It will often occur during an advance to contact and can easily lead to a hasty attack. The meeting engagement differs from the advance to contact in that it occurs unexpectedly whereas in the advance to contact the commander is deliberately seeking to establish contact with the enemy.
Prior intention to commit a criminal act, with the knowledge that the act is a crime.
A true NORTH and SOUTH line.

A message is any thought or idea expressed briefly, in plain or coded language, and prepared in a form suitable for transmission by a means of communication. All messages for transmission over net radio are either:Informal or Formal.a.Informal (or unregistered) messages.Informal messages are transmitted either directly by the originator, or passed verbally or in writing to an operator for transmission. Originators of informal messages for transmission by an operator should write their message down if verbal instructions are likely to cause error or confusion. Written informal messages are not normally drafted on a message form and signed by the originator or registered in amessage centre, but are usually passed directly from originator to operator for transmission.b.Formal (or registered) messages.Formal messages are normally prepared for indirect communication between originators and addressees from different units or formations which are served by separate radio nets or other communications systems. Consequently, the requirement for these messages on most tactical voice nets, particularly at unit level, is minimal.
A message is given a precedence to indicate theorder in which it should be handled. The degrees of precedence are:ROUTINE,PRIORITY,IMMEDIATEandFLASH.

Any message which contains information that may be of value to an enemy must be classified (all others areUNCLASSIFIED). The originator is responsible for ensuring that a message bears the lowest classification consistent with its contents. The categories are:TOP SECRET, SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTEDandUNCLASSIFIED.
An agency responsible for acceptance, transmission,receipt and delivery of msgs.
Military Aid to the Civil Community (MACC).

MACC is the provision of tri- Service personnel and equipment both in emergencies, such as naturaldisasters, and in routine situations to assist the community at large. Examples of this role are the use of EOD bomb disposal units and assisting thecommunity during a civil emergency such as flooding.
Military Aid to the Civil Ministries (MACM).

This encompasses the use of military forces for non-military government tasks, including assistance tomaintain public services and the essentials of life in a community or to undertake urgent work of national importance. Recent examples include firefighting and providing emergency ambulance and prison support services.
Military Aid to the Civil Power (MACP).
MACP is the help the military provides to maintain public order and security when the police are unable to control the situation.

The personal staff officer of a two-star general orappointment of two-star general and above. The nature of duty is not as personal as that of the ADC. It involves chiefly, office work and includes:a. Supervision of work in the office.b. Sorting out all papers addressed to the commander.c. Preparation of notes, papers and speeches for the commander.
Military effectiveness is the standard by which theArmy is judged in peace and war, from platoon to the highest levels.
Military Law is a set of rules and regulations or body of laws for the day-to-day administration of the military disciplinary control of the members of Armed Forces.

Any object which by nature, location, purpose or usemakes an effective contribution to military action and whose total or partial destruction, capture or neutralisation, in the circumstances ruling at the time,offers a definite military advantage.

An explosive or material, normally encased, designed to destroy ordamage ground vehicles, boats or aircraft, or designed to wound, kill or otherwise incapacitate personnel. It may be detonated by the presence, proximity or contact of a person or vehicle, i.e., it must be initiated by its intended target.
Anti-tank mines or an anti-tank mine protected by a number of anti-personnel mines or a group of anti-personnel mines.
A single row of clusters laid in a generally straight line.
Two parallel mine clusters laid simultaneously six paces apart.

In land warfare, minefield is an area of ground containing mines laid with or without a pattern. The types of minefield are:a.Protective Minefield.Used to assist a unit in its local close protection. It is laid by the unit concerned and should be covered by direct fire.b.Tactical Minefield.It is laid to block enemy attack formations in selected areas to deflect his approach into a favourable killing area. It is also used to prevent penetration between positions andstrengthen the defence of the positions. It should be covered by direct indirect fire; it is also called barrier minefield.c.Nuisance Minefield.It is laid to delay and disorganised the enemy and to hinder his use of an area or route. It is laid without pattern.d.Phoney Minefield.It is used to simulate a minefield in an area with the object of deceiving the enemy. Also known as dummy minefield.e.Defensive Minefield.This is minefield laid in accordance with an established plan to prevent penetration between positions and strengthen the defence of the positions themselves. They are laid byengineers, ahead of protective minefields.
The opening of routes through a minefield when notagainst enemy oppositions.
The average number of mines per metre of an area.
A portion of a minefield in which no mines have been laid, or special width, to enable a friendly force pass through in tactical formation. Normally not less than 100m wide.
An un-mined (or de-mined) route through any minefield suitably marked. Lanes will usually be classified as 'Vehicle Lanes' (8 metreswide) or Foot Lanes' (2 metres wide).
A complete written record of all pertinent informationconcerning a minefield, submitted on a standard form (AF 4017A) by the officer in charge of laying operations

Minimum force means the minimum necessary force that is reasonable in any circumstance to achieve the immediate aim. The degree of force can never be reasonable if it is more than that required to achieve the immediate aim. Minimum necessary force does not mean minimum necessary troops. A large number of men deployed at the right time may enable a commander to use less force than he might otherwise have done.

The essence of mission command is to encouragesubordinate commanders to use their initiative to accomplish the mission in line with the superior commander's intent. Mission command provides theapproach in which the commander gives his orders in a manner which enables his subordinates to understand the followings:a.The commander's intentions''“ i.e. what he is trying to achieve.b.Their missions ''“i.e. the effect they are trying to achieve.c.The purpose or intent of their missions in his concept of operation ''“i.e. why they need to achieve their mission.d.Their delegated freedom of action ''“i.e. the limits within which they can work.
A forward air liaison agency for support helicopter commanded by an air force officer.

Mobile defence focuses on the defeat of the attackingforce by permitting it to advance to a position which exposes it to counter attack and envelopment by a mobile striking force. The emphasis is on destroying the enemy rather than retaining or retaking ground.
Mobile reserves are troops earmarked for ejecting that has penetrated a defensive locality/area.
The act of preparing for war or other emergencies through assembling and organising national resources.

The process by which the armed forces or part of it are brought to a state of readiness for war or other national emergency. It includes organizing personnel, supplies and materiel for active military service. It may involve the call up of reservists.
Mobility is the capability of forces to move from one place to another whilst retaining the ability to fulfil their mission. Speed of movement is what is significant in manoeuvre warfare.

MC is an open area through which a force canmanoeuvre in accordance with its tactical doctrine. It is categorized according to the size of unit or formation which can manoeuvre through them,MC may contain ''Slow Go'' areas.
Modulation is the process by which the amplitude, freq or phase of a carrier wave is varied with time in accordance with the wave form of superimposed information, e.g. speech.
A simple petrol bomb. An improvised explosive deviceusually made of a bottle filled with a flammable liquid such as petrol and a wick that is set alight just before it is thrown.
Momentum in military terms, is a measure of the effect that a formation or unit that is moving can have. It is the product of that moving force's size and speed.

The time planned for the explosion of the first of a series of tactical nuclear weapons as part of a specified ground forces operation (or in the caseof a single strike, the time planned for that explosion.)

In conducting IPB, a NAI is an area which will confirm or deny enemy intentions. It serves to focus attention on areas where the enemy must appear if he has chosen a particular course of action (COA). NAIs provide an objective basis for the employment of RISTA assets. Depending on the amount of ground being observed, there may be Point NAIs, e.g. cross-roads, or Area NAIs e.g. a valley.
A table showing when enemy activity may be expected in each NAI and the type of activity expected.
Direction finding to get to a given point or place.
Negotiations take place when two parties with opposing views meet to resolve their differences.

A net identification sign (NIS) is a random, twicedaily-changing, two-letter group (with the exception of CC) allotted to a radio net to provide a concealed reference to the identity of that net. The NIS shouldbe used whenever it is necessary to distinguish between radio nets or, in conjunction with a call sign, to identify a station on a specific net.
The organization in an FTX that deals withexercise casualties with regards to men, vehicles and equipment and the handling of tokens used to represent real stores.
A 'neutral State' is a State formally or in fact not party to a given armed conflict.
Neutralise is to punish a target with fire in order torender it ineffective. Neutralization does not necessarily imply destruction.

A nickname consists of two words neither of which must be a colour. It is used for convenient to refer to a particular matter in which security protection is not required, e.g., a report line. The two words to be paired should each be distinct and not normally associated to avoid being mistaken for a Code word. Bad example are 'WRIST' with 'WATCH' or 'MATCH' with 'BOX'.

A nick number consists of a two-figure number, used to provide low grade security and easy reference to geography locations. Nick numbers are most useful in mobile operations but not in static positions. They should not be used for location states.
NVP is the plan by which all-night surveillancedevices are coordinated over the battle area.

An area into which no fire support or the effects of firesupport are allowed, except: when the establishing HQ temporarily approves fire missions within the NFA on a mission by mission basis; or when an enemyforce within the NFA engages a friendly force - in this case the commander may engage the enemy to defend his force. See also no fire line.

A NFL is a line short of which artillery, aircraft or ships do not fire except on request or approval of the supported commander but beyond which they may fire at any time without danger to friendly troops. Seealso no fire area.

'No Go'' areas are grounds over which manoeuvre of a deployed force is considered impracticable. It must be assessed according to the type of force, for example armour, wheeled and dismounted forces have different requirements and constraints.
That area of ground between two opposing forces which is not physically occupied by either, but which both will endeavour to dominate by means of patrols, observation and similar methods.

A procedure employed during training exercises totransmit 'real' message which are not part of the exercise. The word NODUF is entered in the MESSAGE INSTRUCTIONS box and also at the beginning of the text. For example, if a participant in an exercise gets badly injured and a helicopter is needed for medivac. Such a massage will be a 'NODUF' message.

A night attack where all available fire support is used. This method is employed when there is little chance of achieving surprise by stealth or when it is expedient in the circumstances. Deception measuresshould be planned nevertheless, to conceal the place, scope, direction and timing of the assault.
A NEO is a raid which involves incursion into, and temporary occupation of territory for the purposeof rescuing non-combatants and ends with a planned withdrawal.

Those troops, vehicles and equipment that are determined undesirable or not required during the conduct of a withdrawal operation and should be got rid of early. They are the first elements to withdraw after the Rear Recce Party and may include elements such as cooks, regimental aidpost, etc.

In signal message writing, when the reference of an earlier correspondence (letter or message) is quoted in which not all addresses hold that reference, 'NOTAL' is inserted immediately after the quoted reference. NOTAL means 'not to all'.

Radiations which are invisible, highly penetrating andharmful, that accompany a nuclear explosion. They are emitted in two stages. The first, at the instant of explosion and immediately afterwards calledinitialradiationand the second stage consisting of all radioactive detectable after the first phase and known asresidual radiation.
Warfare involving the employment of nuclear weapons.
Objective is the physical object of the action taken, e.g., a definite tactical feature, the seizure or holding of which is essential to the commander's plan.
A defined geographical area within which is located an objective to be captured or reached by the military forces. This area is definedby competent authority for purposes of command and control.

An observation post is a tactical post, which affordsgood observation to record enemy activity in a given area. Persons manning an observation post must carry pencil, note book, field glasses, compasswatch and a map (if available) in addition to personal weapon. The observation post may be connected by field telephone/radio set with the HQ of their unit/subunit.
An obstacle is a natural or man-made restriction to movement that will normally require special equipment or munitions to overcome it.

Areas where employment of obstacles will normally be controlled at divisional/brigade level. Obstacle beltsare designated within assigned obstacle zones in order to grant obstacles emplacement authority tobrigades and subordinate commands. Obstacle belts should not cross unit boundaries, but more than one may be assigned to a unit.

One or two individual obstacles grouped together toprovide a specific obstacle effect. Battlegroup commanders designate obstacle groups to ensure that manoeuvre companies place individual obstacles that support the battlegroup commander's intent.

Areas where the employment of obstacles will becontrolled at force, corps, or divisional level. Commanders may grant obstacle emplacement authority to brigades and subordinate commands butuse zones to ensure that subordinates place obstacles that support the higher commander's intent and do not interfere with future operations.
To gain possession of and maintain control over a place or region by military action.

OAS has 2 components and they are:a.Battlefield Air Interdiction (BAI).BAI is air action against hostile land targets which are in a position to affect friendly forces directly but which are not yet in contact with them.b.Close Air Support (CAS). CAS is air action against hostile targets in close proximity to friendly forces and requiring positive control to integrate each air mission with ground manoeuvre.

A unit or quantity of supplies adopted as a standard of measurement, used in estimating the average daily expenditure under stated conditions. It may also be expressed in terms of a factor, e.g., rounds of ammunition per weapon per day.

An exercise with troops aimed at making a formationor unit efficient in a particular method of tactical action, and to give commanders and staffs practice in handling troops.
